# MinimalKafka: Guide for AI Agents

> MinimalKafka is a .NET library for Kafka consumers and producers, with
> minimal API-style topic handlers, stream processing, and middleware.
> This guide describes the repository version; check the target package
> version and API reference before generating code for another release.

## Documentation

These links are relative to the published documentation site.

- [Getting started](getting-started.html): installation, configuration, and a
  complete consumer setup.
- [Stream branching](stream-branching.html): route records based on predicates.
- [Resilience](resilience.html): retries, middleware order, cancellation, and
  offset behavior.
- [Dead-letter queues](dead-letter-queues.html): routing, metadata, and current
  payload limitations.
- [Claim-check pattern](claims-check-pattern.html): offload large serialized
  values and restore them on consumption.
- [API reference](api/MinimalKafka.html): public types and members.
- [Repository](https://github.com/pmdevers/MinimalKafka): source, tests, and
  examples.

## Basic consumer

Install the `MinimalKafka` package and configure an accessible Kafka broker and
consumer group. For example, in an ASP.NET Core application's Program.cs:

```csharp
using MinimalKafka;
using MinimalKafka.Attributes;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

builder.Services.AddMinimalKafka(kafka =>
{
    kafka.WithConfiguration(options =>
    {
        options.Common["bootstrap.servers"] = "localhost:19092";
        options.Consumer["group.id"] = "my-app";
        options.Consumer["auto.offset.reset"] = "earliest";
    });
});

var app = builder.Build();

app.MapTopic("my-topic", ([FromKey] string key, [FromValue] string value) =>
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Received: {key} - {value}");
});

await app.RunAsync();
```

`Common` settings apply to consumers and producers; `Consumer` settings apply
to consumers. JSON serialization is registered by default. Use `[FromServices]`
for dependencies resolved from DI; `KafkaContext` and `CancellationToken` are
provided automatically. Handlers return `void` or `Task`.

## Behavior to preserve

- The consumer explicitly commits an offset after the complete consumer
  pipeline succeeds. Unhandled processing failures do not reach that commit.
  Processing and committing are not atomic; design side effects to tolerate
  redelivery.
- Retry and dead-letter policies are opt-in per topic. Use
  `.WithDeadLetter().WithRetry()` when retries should happen before dead-letter
  routing. Middleware registration order changes the behavior.
- The current dead-letter implementation passes the consumed value as the
  producer key and the consumed key as the producer value. Keyless source
  records fail publication. Do not assume the original key/value layout or
  replay DLQ records unchanged; consult the dead-letter guide.
- Claim-check offloads the entire serialized value only when its byte length
  exceeds the configured threshold. Producers and consumers need access to the
  same store and header configuration. Local temporary storage is not shared
  automatically between hosts.

## Working in the repository

- `src/MinimalKafka/` contains the core library; sibling projects provide
  aggregates, dashboard, and RocksDB integrations.
- `examples/` contains runnable usage examples; `test/` contains test projects.
- `docs/` contains feature guides; API reference pages are generated by DocFX.
- The repository targets .NET 10. Run `dotnet build` and `dotnet test` from the
  repository root as appropriate. Kafka-dependent scenarios require an
  accessible broker; do not assume one is running.
- Prefer the current source, tests, and API reference over older examples when
  behavior or signatures differ. Do not invent configuration keys, delivery
  guarantees, or supported APIs.
